XT_UTF_8_CODEC

inherit
	XT_LATIN_1_CODEC
		redefine
			copy_as_utf_8, encoding
		end

create
	make, make_shared, make_empty, make_from_string

feature -- Access

	encoding: INTEGER
		do
			Result := UTF_8
		end

feature -- Basic operations

	copy_as_utf_8 (dest: SPECIAL [CHARACTER]; dest_index, n: INTEGER)
		local
			ptr: POINTER; i, j, i_final: INTEGER; c: CHARACTER
		do
			ptr := area; i_final := count.min (n) - 1
			i := 0; j := dest_index
			if pending_CR then
			-- The last chunked ended with a CR
				inspect c_read_character_8 (ptr, i) when '%N' then
					do_nothing
				else
				-- replace isolated '%R' with '%N'
					dest [j] := '%N'
					i_final := i_final - 1 -- reduce the number of remaining characters
					j := j + 1
				end
				pending_CR := False
			end
			from until i > i_final loop
				c := c_read_character_8 (ptr, i)
				inspect c when '%R' then
					i := i + 1 -- skip '%R'
					if i > i_final then
					-- find out in next chunk if characters is Newline
						pending_CR := True
					else
						inspect c_read_character_8 (ptr, i) when '%N' then
							do_nothing
						else
						-- replace isolated '%R' with '%N'
							dest [j] := '%N'
							j := j + 1
						end
					end
				else
					dest [j] := c
					j := j + 1
					i := i + 1
				end
			end
			last_index := i
			utf_8_copied_count := j - dest_index
			set_utf_8_to_count_ratio
		end

prepare_buffer (a_count: INTEGER): BOOLEAN
			-- Ensure `buffer' has room for `a_count' more bytes
			-- after `buffer_end'.  Compacts or reallocates as needed,
			-- preserving up to `Context_bytes' before `buffer_index' for
			-- error reporting.  Returns False and sets `error_code' on
			-- failure; buffer indices are adjusted consistently on success.
			--
			-- Corresponds to the resize/compact logic in XML_GetBuffer().
		local
			needed, parsed, keep, offset, new_size: INTEGER
		do
			if a_count <= buffer_limit - buffer_end then
				-- Enough free space after buffer_end already.
				Result := True
			else
				parsed := buffer_index                 -- bytes before buffer_ptr
				keep   := parsed.min (Context_bytes)   -- context bytes to retain
				needed := keep + a_count + (buffer_end - buffer_index)

				if needed < 0 then
					-- Integer overflow: the request is impossibly large.
					error_code := Error_no_memory

				elseif needed <= buffer_limit then
					-- Existing allocation fits once we compact.
					offset := parsed - keep
					if offset > 0 then
						shift_buffer_left (offset)
					end
					Result := True

				else
					-- Must grow. Double from current capacity until large enough.
					new_size := buffer_limit.max (Default_buffer_size)

EiffelStudio 25.02.9.8723 Enterprise and MSVC 19.44.35229 on Windows x64. The
campaign retained all **5,170 engine/case rows** and returned Python exit 1,
`complete_with_failures`, for the observed core results:

| Implementation | Passed | Wrong verdicts | Timeouts | Excluded |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| xpact | 1,727 | 0 | 0 | 858 |
| pinned Xpact-core | 1,051 | 662 | 14 | 858 |

Core's wrong verdicts comprise 339 false accepts and 323 false rejects. For
example, `rmt-ns10-025` and `rmt-ns10-026` contain unbound element/attribute
prefixes: core accepted both with namespaces enabled, while xpact rejected
them. Core rejected the original big-endian UTF-16 document `utf16b`; xpact
accepted it as required. UTF-16 does not explain the broad false-reject count:
312 of those 323 cases are in `eduni/errata-4e`, covering fifth-edition name
changes. These are observations; this change does not repair the pinned parser.

All 14 process errors were ten-second timeouts with empty stdout/stderr, on
30–295-byte malformed inputs. For example, `not-wf-sa-055` contains an unfinished
DOCTYPE/internal subset and `o-p24fail1` has mismatched XML-version quotes.
Their internal cause remains unconfirmed. They are not normal rejections or
demonstrated crashes.

Both assertion configurations gave the same directed results: xpact passed

namespace and reuse-sequence controls. The reuse sequence includes an unbound
prefix check, so its failure does not independently establish a recovery defect.

data.kind: read-only source audit; no builds, tests, or timings executed
data.line_reference_scope: XP_PARSER line numbers refer to the actual selected parser with identical bytes in repo/src and the recorded doctype/src snapshot. Initial broad and inactive prototype identities are excluded.
data.narrowed_candidate_lifetime: The actual selected rule enables DOCTYPE slices only for the exact detachable XP_NULL_EVENT_HANDLER dynamic type with no external resolver, no active entity, a default-or-smaller attribute cap and all retained common guards. Newly enabled slices reference normalized document input already retained by position_input. General entity entry pushes entity_stack before parse_entity_content (2664/2665 and 2733/2734), so replacement tags do not use the new DOCTYPE case. Existing no-DOCTYPE behavior is preserved.

findings.observation: open_element_range creates XP_TOKEN_SLICE(a_input,start,count); the slice owns a strong reference to its complete source buffer, not just the token bytes. It is pushed together with a shared marker. A slice over resolver-returned entity text can therefore retain that entire replacement buffer.

close_element_range validates entity floor and exact name match, then pop_open_element removes the slice when slice and element stack counts are equal and removes the marker. A completed balanced document has no active element slices. Standard container capacity remains allocated.

Parse errors do not unwind element stacks. A mismatch, unclosed tag, depth-limit failure or entity error leaves already-open slices active until explicit reset or next parse/replay reset. Newly enabled DOCTYPE slices refer only to normalized document input already retained by position_input. The actual exact-null/no-resolver/no-active-entity guard excludes a new retaining path to raw resolver-returned buffers. Slice-object release remains separate from buffer retention.

reset_for_reuse delegates to reset. reset creates an empty position_input, wipes both element stacks and entity/declaration tables, and clears cached DOCTYPE references. Next ordinary parse invokes reset before normalization. This removes the parser's active references to failed slices and replacement buffers, apart from user/resolver references outside the parser.

reset_cached_doctype_body wipes both element stacks and reference stacks before replay, while intentionally retaining DTD declaration/entity tables and snapshots. Caller then installs a fresh combined position_input. A failed body parse calls clear_cached_doctype, which clears snapshots but does not itself reset active open slices, position_input, or entity tables; they remain until the next reset/replay.

Installed ARRAYED_STACK.remove delegates to ARRAYED_LIST.remove, which invokes SPECIAL.remove_tail -> keep_head -> set_count. wipe_out likewise only sets SPECIAL count to zero. eif_built_in.h defines set_count as assignment to RT_SPECIAL_COUNT. These operations do not physically null unused capacity slots. This audit has not inspected the installed GC implementation or run reclamation tests, so it does not use physical non-null slot bytes alone as proof of a retention leak or prove reclamation from count alone.

position_input deliberately retains the normalized document after both successful and failed parse for diagnostic positions. Internal entity_table and completed-DOCTYPE cache may also intentionally retain values. A weak-reference test on the whole document after success cannot isolate slice release while position_input still points to it.

testing_without_production_api.private_state: A test descendant can inspect inherited XP_PARSER private stacks. ARRAYED_STACK.area is exported only to ARRAYED_STACK clients, so a parser descendant alone cannot call area. A test-only ARRAYED_STACK descendant may re-export area and be installed by the test parser; alternatively REFLECTED_REFERENCE_OBJECT can find area_v2 by field_name and read reference_field.
testing_without_production_api.backing_storage: Check SPECIAL.count and active entries using normal contracts. Reading stale items beyond count is outside SPECIAL.item's valid-index contract and is not a valid assertion-on test; do not expect unused slots to be physically Void.
testing_without_production_api.reclamation: Use test-only WEAK_REFERENCE[XP_TOKEN_SLICE] and, for external replacement text, WEAK_REFERENCE[STRING_8]. Construct/parse/capture weak references in a helper that returns before MEMORY.full_collect, keep parser alive, and drop strong locals, reflection objects and stack snapshots before collection. Check slice existence separately from buffer existence.
sequences: success with DOCTYPE, nested/empty elements and balanced external-entity markup -> no active slices; weak slice becomes reclaimable while parser remains alive
DOCTYPE failure inside resolver-returned replacement text -> replacement tags remain materialized under the new guard; inspect any outer document slice separately; reset_for_reuse -> no active slices
failure -> reset -> valid parse -> second failure -> reset; inspect separate weak references from each generation
cached DOCTYPE non-final body with open elements -> cached replay replaces old active slices; final success -> no active slices
cached DOCTYPE failed body -> snapshots cleared but active slices retained until next reset/replay
grow beyond initial stack capacity32 -> pop all -> reset; count0 and reclaimability, with capacity retention allowed
testing_without_production_api.runtime_scope: Run assertions on/off and native session reset/dispose paths when authorized. Managed .NET GC requires its own check; installed EiffelBase source chain audited here is native ELKS.

data.conclusion: No new source-level use-after-pop or missed-reset path identified. Actual selected eligibility creates DOCTYPE slices only over normalized document input that position_input already retains; failed active slices remain until the existing reset boundary. Slice-object reclamation needs a separate weak-reference test. Standard remove/wipe_out shrinks SPECIAL.count without physically clearing unused capacity slots.

    if isinstance(value, list):

    return rel(value) if isinstance(value, str) and Path(value).is_absolute() else value

def publish(outputs):
    staged, published = [], []
    try:
        for destination, payload in outputs:
            if destination.exists():
                need(destination.read_bytes() == payload, "Preserving existing different evidence: " + str(destination))
                continue
            descriptor, temporary = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".pubmed-doctype-", dir=destination.parent)
            with os.fdopen(descriptor, "wb") as stream:
                stream.write(payload)
                stream.flush()
                os.fsync(stream.fileno())
            staged.append((Path(temporary), destination, hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest()))
        for temporary, destination, digest in staged:
            need(not destination.exists(), "Publication target appeared concurrently")
            temporary.replace(destination)
            published.append((destination, digest))
    except BaseException:
        for destination, digest in reversed(published):
            if destination.exists() and hashlib.sha256(destination.read_bytes()).hexdigest() == digest:
                destination.unlink()
        raise
    finally:
        for temporary, _, _ in staged:
            temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)

def fingerprint(row):
    return tuple(row[key] for key in ("actual", "status", "category", "returncode"))


def compare_one(case, dataset, build, paths, timeout, work, known):
    # Each case and engine has its own crash-output directory, including in parallel runs.
    case_work = work / hashlib.sha256((dataset + case.id).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:20]
    case_work.mkdir()
    observed = {}
    for role, executable in paths.items():
        role_work = case_work / role
        role_work.mkdir()
        observed[role] = observe(case, build, role, executable, timeout, role_work, known)
    baseline, candidate = observed["baseline"], observed["candidate"]
    outcome_match = fingerprint(baseline) == fingerprint(candidate)
    stdout_match = baseline["stdout_hex"] == candidate["stdout_hex"]
    return {"dataset": dataset, "build": build, "case_id": case.id, "path": str(case.path),
            "outcome_match": outcome_match, "stdout_match": stdout_match,
            "match": outcome_match and (dataset != "directed" or stdout_match), **observed}

class

inherit

create
	make

feature {NONE} -- Command line

	make
		local
			l_arguments: ARGUMENTS_32
			l_path: detachable STRING_32
			i, l_iterations: INTEGER
			l_has_iterations, l_invalid: BOOLEAN
		do
			create l_arguments
			from i := 1 until i > l_arguments.argument_count or l_invalid loop
				if l_arguments.argument (i).same_string ("--iterations") and not l_has_iterations and then i < l_arguments.argument_count and then l_arguments.argument (i + 1).is_integer then
					l_iterations := l_arguments.argument (i + 1).to_integer
					l_has_iterations := True
					i := i + 2
				elseif l_arguments.argument (i).same_string ("--file") and l_path = Void and then i < l_arguments.argument_count and then not l_arguments.argument (i + 1).is_empty then
					l_path := l_arguments.argument (i + 1).twin
					i := i + 2
				else
					l_invalid := True
				end
			end
			if l_invalid or not l_has_iterations or l_iterations <= 0 then
				io.error.put_string ("usage: --iterations POSITIVE_INTEGER [--file PATH]%N")
				exit_with_code (2)
			elseif attached l_path as l_file_path then
				if attached raw_file_bytes (l_file_path) as l_document then
					benchmark (l_document, l_iterations)
				else
					io.error.put_string ("benchmark cannot read complete XML file%N")
					exit_with_code (2)
				end
			elseif catalog.count = 2611 then
				benchmark (catalog, l_iterations)
			else
				io.error.put_string ("unexpected catalog fixture length%N")
				exit_with_code (2)
			end
		end

	benchmark (a_document: STRING_8; a_iterations: INTEGER)
			-- Prepare one backend and repeatedly parse the same immutable bytes.
		local
			l_backend: DC_BACKEND
			i: INTEGER
			l_ok: BOOLEAN
		do
			create l_backend.make (False)
			from i := 0; l_ok := True until i = a_iterations or not l_ok loop
				l_ok := l_backend.parse (a_document)
				if l_ok then i := i + 1 end
			end
			if l_ok and i = a_iterations then
				l_backend.close
				io.put_string ("xpact benchmark harness parsed " + i.out + " documents.%N")
			else
				io.error.put_string ("file benchmark failed after " + i.out + " documents: " + l_backend.last_error + "%N")
				l_backend.close
				exit_with_code (1)
			end
		end

	raw_file_bytes (a_path: READABLE_STRING_GENERAL): detachable STRING_8
			-- Read original bytes once; preserve BOMs, encodings and line endings.
		local
			l_file: RAW_FILE
			l_expected_count: INTEGER
		do
			create l_file.make_with_name (a_path)
			if l_file.exists and then l_file.is_plain and then l_file.is_readable then
				l_file.open_read
				l_expected_count := l_file.count
				create Result.make (l_expected_count)
				from until Result.count >= l_expected_count or else l_file.end_of_file loop
					l_file.read_stream (65536)
					Result.append (l_file.last_string)
				end
				l_file.close
				if Result.count /= l_expected_count then Result := Void end
			end
		rescue
			io.error.put_string ("benchmark file read failed%N")
			exit_with_code (2)
		end

	exit_with_code (a_code: INTEGER)
		local
			l_exceptions: EXCEPTIONS
		do
			create l_exceptions
			l_exceptions.die (a_code)
		end

end
